title: Merrick and Massapequa: A Local Account of Refuge
summary: A Baldwin local history remembers Massapequa people offering refuge to Merrick families displaced by colonial settlement.
address_label: Regional Merrick–Massapequa history; no identified parcel
ancestral_territory_note: Linked to Merrick Ancestral Land with recognition of overlapping Merikoke/Merrick and Massapequa histories.
why_this_matters: Displacement also brought people into relationships of refuge and support. This local account remembers connections between neighboring Native communities during colonial expansion.
introduction_title: Refuge in a Later Local History
introduction_content:
Baldwin: Our Heritage, published in 1976, describes Massapequa people offering refuge to Merrick families displaced by colonial settlement in Kings County. The account places Merrick or Merikoke homes between Parsonage Creek and Fort Neck Creek.1

This remembered relationship places the history of refuge and mutual support alongside the history of land loss.1
history_content:
Refuge within a network of neighbors

The local account in Baldwin: Our Heritage foregrounds a relationship between Merrick and Massapequa people: families making room for others under pressure from colonial settlement. Its value lies in preserving a memory of mutual support, as well as displacement. It is a later local account, written long after the events it describes.1

Seventeenth-century land records provide a different window into the same regional connections. Masepeage, Merriack, and Rockaway appear together in the 1643 deed tradition, while Tackapousha and other Native representatives later challenged Hempstead’s claims to Mercock. These documents show communities acting through negotiations and testimony as well as through their relationships with neighbors.23

The 1742 Merrick journal entry carries the story forward: a Native community remained part of the South Shore network well after the earliest agreements. Read together, the local remembrance and the dated records make continued community life visible.4
whereintheworld_content: The account belongs to the intertwined histories of Merrick and Massapequa on Long Island’s South Shore.
